name: Christian Stocker
role: Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria (Bundeskanzler)
bio: Christian Stocker, born in Wiener Neustadt in 1960, a law graduate (Dr. iur.) of the University of Vienna and a lawyer there since 1994, has been Federal Chancellor of Austria since 3 March 2025, heading a coalition of his Austrian People's Party (ÖVP) with the Social Democrats (SPÖ) and NEOS, the first federal government to include NEOS. A municipal politician for three decades, he sat on Wiener Neustadt's city council from 1990 and was its vice-mayor from 2000 to 2025, entered the National Council in 2019, became ÖVP secretary-general under Karl Nehammer in September 2022 and was named acting party leader on 5 January 2025, after Nehammer resigned when the first ÖVP–SPÖ–NEOS talks failed; a party congress elected him chairman with 98.42% on 29 March 2025. On taking over the party he dropped the ÖVP's refusal to govern under Herbert Kickl, whose FPÖ had won the September 2024 election, but the ÖVP–FPÖ talks broke down on 12 February 2025 and a second round of three-party negotiations made him Chancellor. As of October 2026 his government's record includes two double budgets aimed at consolidating public finances, with an EU excessive deficit procedure opened in July 2025 and the goal of a 3% deficit in 2028, a suspension of family reunification for refugees, a headscarf ban for schoolgirls under 14, messenger surveillance of suspected extremists, a tighter gun law after the Graz school shooting of June 2025 and a pension reform; in October 2026 an FPÖ motion of no confidence in the government failed, and Stocker testified before the parliamentary inquiry into the death of former senior justice official Christian Pilnacek.
